text:
Washington and Ottawa both arrive on the heels of one-goal-margin wins and a three-day layoff. The Capitals (3-2-0 in their last five) beat Florida 4-3 on Saturday, when Jack St. Ivany scored his first NHL goal, though they're without Vincent Desharnais. The Senators (3-1-1) beat Utah 4-2 and are missing Andre Burakovsky, Warren Foegele and William Eklund. With Eklund out, Tim Stützle has moved beside Cozens and Zetterlund, and Ridly Greig is up to 18:32 a night from 16:00. Greig could return tonight, as ESPN has cleared him from its injury report.

There is little to separate them. At five on five, WSH has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and OTT 52%, and our model has it 3.22 to 3.18 for the Senators. The special-teams matchup to watch is Ottawa's power play, which creates 0.76 expected goals a game, against Washington's penalty kill, which allows 0.87. The Senators also take 4.7 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays. In net, Logan Thompson (projected) is at +1.9 goals saved above expected this season and +28.2 in 58 games last year. Samuel Ersson (projected) is at -0.3, after -17.8 last season, though he has saved 3.9 goals above expected over his last five starts.

We like Alex Tuch, who has a 39% chance to score and was just flagged as due to cool. Stützle has a 36% chance to score and a 77% chance at a point, and Drake Batherson is at 33% to score. Alex Ovechkin is pointless in seven straight despite 3.3 expected goals, so the chances are there. Ryan Leonard plays his 100th NHL game.
